title: From Bamboo Cracks to Flower Fire: The Long Story of Festival Fireworks
title_zh: 从爆竹到花火：节日烟花的漫长故事
intro_zh: 本文约561词，共9段，讲述节日烟花的由来：中国古代村民烧竹子发出的爆响、炼金术士偶然发现火药、李畋与浏阳的爆竹、烟花沿着贸易路线西传、金属盐带来的缤纷色彩、日本的“花火”，以及今天无人机带来的新变化。文中共含6个CET-4核心词，句子难度中等偏易，适合四级阅读练习。

paragraphs.en: On the last night of the year, millions of people look up at the same time. A bright explosion opens like a flower and falls as golden rain. Fireworks feel modern, but their story began more than a thousand years ago in ancient China.
paragraphs.zh: 在一年最后一个夜晚，数以百万计的人同时仰望天空。一朵明亮的爆炸像花一样绽开，又化作金色的雨落下。烟花看起来很现代，但它的故事始于一千多年前的古代中国。

paragraphs.en: Long before anyone had gunpowder, Chinese villagers noticed something strange. When they threw green bamboo into a fire, the air inside the sealed joints heated up and burst out with a loud crack. The sound seemed to frighten away evil spirits. People called these bursting sticks 'baozhu', and for centuries they were the only fireworks in the world.
paragraphs.zh: 在还没有火药的很久以前，中国村民注意到一件怪事。当他们把青竹扔进火里时，竹节内部被封住的空气受热膨胀，随着一声巨响爆裂开来。这声音似乎能把恶鬼吓跑。人们把这种会爆裂的竹竿叫作“爆竹”，此后几百年间，它们是世界上唯一的“烟花”。

paragraphs.en: The next step came from a search that failed. Around 1,300 years ago, Chinese alchemists were trying to make a medicine that would let people live forever. They mixed three common substances: saltpeter, sulfur and charcoal. Instead of a magic potion, they produced a powder that burned very fast. Because it was made from three medicines, or 'fire medicines', it was named huoyao. Today we call it gunpowder.
paragraphs.zh: 下一步来自一次失败的探索。大约1300年前，中国的炼金术士试图制造一种能让人长生不老的药。他们把三种常见物质混在一起：硝石、硫磺和木炭。得到的不是神奇的灵药，而是一种燃烧极快的粉末。因为它由三种“药”制成，所以被称为“火药”。今天我们叫它 gunpowder。

paragraphs.en: According to tradition, a man named Li Tian from Liuyang, in Hunan province, made the first firecracker around 800 AD. He packed the powder into a bamboo tube and lit a fuse. His neighbors were amazed, and later generations honored him as the father of fireworks. Liuyang still makes fireworks today; the small city sends its products to more than 100 countries.
paragraphs.zh: 按照传说，公元800年前后，湖南浏阳一位名叫李畋的人做出了最早的爆竹。他把这种粉末装进竹筒，点燃引线。邻居们惊叹不已，后世尊他为烟花之父。直到今天浏阳仍在生产烟花；这座小城把产品销往100多个国家。

paragraphs.en: From China the new invention traveled west along trade routes. Arab merchants carried the knowledge across Asia, and by the 13th century Europeans knew both gunpowder and fireworks. One popular story says Marco Polo brought them home, though historians doubt it. In Europe, Italy took the lead. Italian craftsmen turned fireworks into an art form, and by the 17th century kings and cities were paying for huge shows to mark victories, weddings and birthdays.
paragraphs.zh: 这项新发明沿着贸易路线向西传播。阿拉伯商人把知识带过亚洲，到13世纪，欧洲人已同时知晓火药和烟花。有一个流行的说法是马可·波罗把它们带回了家，不过历史学家对此表示怀疑。在欧洲，意大利走在前列。意大利工匠把烟花变成了一种艺术，到17世纪，国王和城市都愿意花钱办盛大的表演来庆祝胜利、婚礼和生日。

paragraphs.en: For a long time, however, all fireworks looked orange or gold, because that is the color of burning charcoal. Beautiful colors only arrived in the 19th century, when chemists learned to add metal salts to the mixture. Strontium gives red, copper gives blue, barium gives green and sodium gives bright yellow. The trick is the same one students meet in a simple flame test: heat makes each metal release its own special light.
paragraphs.zh: 然而在很长一段时间里，所有烟花都是橙色或金色的，因为那是木炭燃烧的颜色。绚丽的色彩直到19世纪才出现，当时化学家学会在混合物中加入金属盐。锶产生红色，铜产生蓝色，钡产生绿色，钠产生明黄色。其中的原理和学生在简单焰色试验中学到的一样：受热会让每种金属释放出自己特有的光。

paragraphs.en: Fireworks reached Japan in the 16th century, and the Japanese gave them one of their loveliest names: hanabi, which means 'flower fire'. In 1733, a fireworks festival was held beside the Sumida River in Edo, now Tokyo, to comfort people after a year of hunger and disease. That festival still takes place every summer, and hanabi has become a word that suggests summer itself.
paragraphs.zh: 烟花在16世纪传到日本，日本人给了它最美妙的名字之一：hanabi（花火），意思是“花之火”。1733年，人们在江户（今东京）的隅田川旁举办烟花大会，以抚慰经历了一年饥荒与疾病的人们。这一大会至今每年夏天仍会举行，而“花火”也成了让人想到夏天本身的词。

paragraphs.en: Modern displays have grown astonishing. The largest single shell ever fired weighed more than 1,000 kilograms and climbed nearly one kilometer into the sky. Yet fireworks also bring problems: smoke, noise, injuries and frightened animals. Some cities now replace them with light shows performed by hundreds of small drones. Others keep the old tradition, but with stricter safety rules and quieter, cleaner powders.
paragraphs.zh: 现代的烟花表演已经令人惊叹。有史以来发射过的最大单颗礼花弹重逾1000公斤，升空近一公里。但烟花也带来问题：烟雾、噪音、受伤以及受惊的动物。如今一些城市用数百架小型无人机表演的灯光秀取而代之。另一些城市保留这一古老传统，但采用更严格的安全规定和更安静、更清洁的火药。

paragraphs.en: Why do we still love them? Perhaps because a firework is a short, bright lesson. It appears without warning, gives everything it has in two seconds, and disappears. Every festival, people light a fuse for the same reasons their ancestors did: to say goodbye to the old year, to welcome the new, and to fill the dark sky with hope.
paragraphs.zh: 我们为什么依然喜爱烟花？也许因为烟花就是一堂短暂而明亮的课。它毫无预兆地出现，在两秒钟里倾尽所有，然后消失。每逢节日，人们点燃引线，理由和他们的祖先一样：告别旧岁，迎接新年，让黑暗的天空充满希望。

questions.q: According to the passage, why did the earliest Chinese 'fireworks' make a loud crack?
options: Villagers burned a pot of gunpowder in the yard.
Air sealed inside heated bamboo joints burst out.
Alchemists threw their medicine into a stove.
People hit bamboo sticks against stones.
questions.explain: 第二段明确说明：村民把青竹扔进火里，竹节内部被封住的空气受热膨胀并爆裂，发出巨响。A、C、D 均未在文中出现，属于无据选项。

questions.q: What does the passage say about the alchemists who produced gunpowder?
options: They were trying to make a medicine for long life.
They wanted to build stronger weapons for war.
They were ordered by the emperor to make fireworks.
They copied the recipe from Arab traders.
questions.explain: 第三段指出，炼金术士本意是制造让人长生不老的药，却意外得到燃烧极快的粉末。文中未提到武器、皇帝命令或抄袭阿拉伯配方。

questions.q: The writer mentions drones in the eighth paragraph mainly to show that ___.
options: fireworks are no longer popular in modern cities
technology has completely replaced traditional festivals
some cities are looking for cleaner ways to celebrate
drones are much cheaper than fireworks
questions.explain: 第八段先说烟花带来烟雾、噪音等问题，接着说有些城市用无人机灯光秀替代烟花，有些城市则保留传统但使用更清洁的火药。可见提到的目的是说明一些城市在寻找更清洁的庆祝方式，而非说烟花不受欢迎或无人机更便宜。

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main idea of the passage?
options: Fireworks are dangerous and should be banned in cities.
Fireworks began in China and spread worldwide, changing with chemistry and culture.
Only Chinese people understand the true meaning of fireworks.
Metal salts are the most important part of modern fireworks.
questions.explain: 全文从中国古代烧竹、火药偶然发现、李畋与浏阳，写到烟花传入欧洲、日本以及今天的变化，主旨是烟花的起源与全球传播及其在化学与文化上的演变。A、C、D 都是以偏概全或文中并未主张的观点。
